newsitem.title: CHINA: China experts prepare plans to cope with disasters.
newsitem.headline: China experts prepare plans to cope with disasters.

text.p: Chinese experts have approved national guidelines aimed at boosting efforts to cope with floods, droughts, fires, earthquakes and other disasters ravaging the nation every year, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
The guideline document was based on a review of major disasters since China's 1949 communist revolution and would be an important reference for policy makers, the newspaper said.
Over the last 48 years, disasters caused China average annual economic losses of 50 billion-60 billion yuan ($6.0 billion-$7.2 billion at current exchange rates), it said.

Disasters killed between 10,000 and 20,000 people in China a year and cost between one-sixth and one-fourth of national revenues, it quoted Sun Yongjian of the State Science and Technology Commission as saying, but gave no details.
The new guideline on disaster alleviation had been approved by experts from eight central governent ministries and departments, the China Daily said.

China would establish networks to guide disaster prevention in urban areas and enterprises while developing new laws and finding ways to boost funding of disaster alleviation projects, it quoted Sun as saying.
